findings.claim: The implementation Worker is the main entry point for optional agentic mechanisms: runAgentLoop accepts experiment-only flags for subagents, MCP repository reads, A2A impact delegation, memory hints, and conversation-state transport; phase gating limits MCP/A2A to implementation, while subagents are enabled only when explicitly true.

Bounded research subagents enter when the implementation Worker is given subagentsEnabled=true. The Worker receives delegate_research in addition to normal target-app tools, and at most one delegation is permitted (MAX_RESEARCH_DELEGATIONS=1). The child is selected by research model routing, capped at six turns, and receives only list_files/read_file plus submit_evidence_report. Child reports are provenance-admitted against observed reads and returned as advisory observations.

Research-child authority is deliberately non-authoritative: handoff and observation state that the child cannot write, run commands, delegate, expand the Spec, grant permissions, or declare success; EvidenceReport is advisory and not Spec, permission, verification, or workflow success. Outer Worker/harness retains implementation responsibility and verification authority.

The optional A2A remote impact-analysis mechanism is entered by adding delegate_remote_analysis to the implementation Worker tool set. The Worker is instructed to call it once before its first write, and the loop maintains a one-call budget. The model supplies only objective and scope; host code chooses endpoint, credentials, process, protocol, and policy.

A2A host-side admission is authoritative: it bounds scope under target-app, discovers/admits an agent card, sends only objective/scope, polls a bounded task, and validates the returned ImpactAnalysis artifact against allowed scope before exposing it as evidence. Records explicitly set grantsWorkflowSuccess=false; rejected, incomplete, or uncertain remote results are not accepted as evidence.

The optional MCP repository-read path is entered by mcpRepoReadEnabled during implementation. The host starts a stdio server with an absolute host-configured allowed root, discovers tools, admits only the allowlisted repo_read_file with a strict schema, and replaces direct read_file in the Worker tool list. Repair/review remain direct-tool paths per run-level contract.

MCP authority remains with the host: the model cannot select the root, the server refuses OPENAI_API_KEY in its environment, path resolution is constrained to the host root, and host admission rejects tools/schemas exposing root or credential controls. The Worker receives read capability only, not write, command, or workflow authority.

Conversation-state chaining is an opt-in episode-local orchestration mechanism. ConversationStateMode can be manual or previous_response_id; the loop tracks previous response IDs and client input metrics, while the orchestration experiment compares three trials per arm and requires correctness, intact tool observability, replay reduction, and no clear regression. The experiment's decision implementation deliberately leaves passed=false, so it does not auto-adopt the variant.

The optional planner is a separate read-only model phase entered when planning is enabled in runV1Harness. buildPlan gives the planner list_files/read_file and submit_plan, admits a parsed Plan, and the run then uses that plan to shape implementation. Planning is explicitly experiment-only and default architecture has no explicit Planner; the resolved Spec and outer workflow remain authoritative.

Review decomposition is an optional advisory mechanism: a harness-owned binder creates/admits a ReviewPlan against the Spec, and formatWorkerUnitTask supplies a current-unit execution scope plus deferred units. The ReviewPlan is explicitly not Spec, permission, or success criteria; unit verification gates continuation, and default remains one Worker.

Bounded fan-out is optional harness-owned process control rather than autonomous model authority. An admitted FanOutPlan requires an exact base commit, exactly two units, no inter-unit dependencies, and Spec acceptance coverage. executeFanOut creates isolated child workspaces, runs children sequentially or in parallel, captures deltas, requires scoped verification, and fans changes into a separate integration workspace in declared order.

Fan-out outer authority is retained through exact-base provenance checks, child verification gating, conflict/lost-change detection, and fan-in ordering. Child prompts explicitly prohibit sibling implementation and identify the full Spec as authoritative; fan-out does not grant new product semantics or permissions.

Verified repository memory is optional and advisory. runV1Harness documents that default runs do not read/write memory and memory cannot change WorkflowState; retrieval filters repository scope, validates current implementation surfaces, rejects stale/mismatched records, and injects at most a formatted hint. The hint states the Spec and current repository remain authoritative.

Spec construction and independent Review are model-driven phases but not authority transfers: Spec phase exposes only read tools plus submit_spec and enforces a SpecDecision; Review exposes only submit_review and receives Spec, diff, constraints, and verification evidence. The outer run owns workflow status and final verification, while the loop documentation says a terminal model response is not verified workflow completion.

uncertainties: The read of loop.ts was harness-truncated before the full executeWorkerTool implementation; exact per-call handling details for delegate_research, MCP calls, and A2A result insertion were inferred from the visible setup/contracts and companion modules, not the omitted body.
This inventory focuses on harness/src runtime mechanisms and does not claim every experiment or probe outside the reviewed files is an independently active execution path.

Durability/lease/retry controls were not treated as agentic mechanisms because they primarily govern workflow persistence and retries rather than granting model capabilities; they may still affect outer execution authority.

report.objective: Audit how optional/experimental agentic mechanisms are exposed, activated, gated, and selected. Determine default versus opt-in versus conditional behavior, who makes adoption decisions, and what repository evidence supports those claims. Identify discrepancies or ambiguities between package/config surfaces, tests, and documentation.

findings.claim: The documented/default execution path is conservative: targeted context → read-only Spec/ambiguity gate → one implementation Worker → deterministic VERIFY/repair → independent REVIEW/repair; experimental mechanisms are not implied by their presence in source.

Optional mechanisms are explicitly opt-in at the run API: `runV1Harness` options include planningEnabled, subagentsEnabled, mcpRepoReadEnabled, a2aDelegationEnabled, memory, review/fan-out binders, admittedSpec, and durable; comments identify Planner/Subagents/MCP/A2A/memory/fan-out as experiment-only or opt-in, while absent durable means in-memory workflow.

The benchmark runner preserves opt-in semantics by defaulting conversation state to manual and passing MCP/A2A only when each option is exactly true. Its BenchmarkRunOptions exposes these switches rather than enabling them globally.

Repository architecture records adoption decisions: Planner, bounded research Subagent, and parallel fan-out are kept OFF by default; decomposition is conditional (not default); previous_response_id remains selectable experimental; verified repository memory is a mechanism probe; durable checkpoints and post-terminal GitHub delivery are opt-in; MCP repo-read and A2A are optional/off by default.

The progress document independently summarizes the same policy: normal flow remains one Worker; previous_response_id, Planner, Subagents, ReviewPlan, durability, delivery, fan-out, MCP, memory, A2A, and SWM01 are all optional seams or probes, with explicit default-off statements for most. It says SWM01 is not called from runV1Harness and has no adoption claim.

The harness, not the model, makes the key adoption/authority decisions: architecture assigns outer harness ownership of whether implementation may start, routing, retry budgets, VERIFY/REVIEW transitions, escalation, workflow success/failure, and trace/eval truth; reviewer and worker have narrower roles.

Subagent tests directly verify default-off exposure: with subagentsEnabled false, delegate_research is absent and the normal four tools are exposed; even when enabled, repair and review_repair do not receive the research tool. Child capability is physically limited to list_files/read_file/submit_evidence_report.

MCP is opt-in and narrowly scoped: the MCP probe calls runBenchmark with mcpRepoReadEnabled true and checks host admission/replacement of direct reads; the test confirms enabling it removes direct read_file while retaining writes and normal tools. No default-on behavior is shown.

A2A is opt-in and externally gated: the probe requires A2A_REMOTE_OPENAI_API_KEY and otherwise exits without falling back to OPENAI_API_KEY, then passes a2aDelegationEnabled true. Its success criteria require accepted advisory delegation but explicitly require grantsWorkflowSuccess=false; tests verify admission/scope/artifact failures and remote task identity.

Memory is opt-in by explicit MemoryRunOptions (promotion/retrieval in the MEM01 probe), and tests enforce that memory is advisory, scope-validated, stale-rejected, and does not modify WorkflowState. The normal tool set remains available.

Durability is opt-in and mutually constrained with experimental paths: tests invoke durable explicitly and assert planningEnabled and memory retrieval/promotion are rejected as unsupported modes. Architecture says default runV1Harness remains in-memory.

Model routing is default-model-first and harness-owned: tests show every episode uses config.model absent repairModel, while OPENAI_REPAIR_MODEL is an optional config override affecting only verification repair. Model selection does not alter write authority/tool permissions.

Package/config/documentation surfaces are incomplete or asymmetric: harness/package.json exposes many optional experiment scripts (experiment, routing, orchestration, planning, subagents, fanout, durability, checkpoint, retry, ownership, MCP, memory, A2A, SWM), but root package.json forwards only a subset (notably no root scripts for planning, orchestration, subagents, durability/checkpoint/retry/ownership/MCP/A2A/SWM); README documents only generic setup and benchmark invocation; .env.example documents OPENAI credentials/GitHub token/delivery issue but not OPENAI_REPAIR_MODEL or A2A_REMOTE_OPENAI_API_KEY or memory/MCP switches.

uncertainties: The full run-benchmark CLI argument parser was truncated by the repository reader, so this audit confirms API/probe/script activation surfaces but cannot exhaustively enumerate every supported CLI flag or determine whether all harness package scripts map cleanly to parser branches.

Architecture/progress are documentation evidence of adoption status rather than runtime proof for every option; deterministic tests strongly cover defaults for subagents, routing, durability, MCP, A2A, and memory but do not constitute a full end-to-end matrix for all experiment binders.
The README's generic benchmark command may permit hidden flags, but it does not document optional mechanism activation or their gating prerequisites.

report.objective: Audit the evidence, artifact, lifecycle, and durability implications of every relevant optional/experimental agentic mechanism. Determine what each returns, how results/errors/state are recorded or propagated, whether execution is durably resumable/persistent, and what outer-harness authority remains after delegation. Clearly mark unsupported or unverified conclusions.

findings.claim: Durable execution persists only a narrow workflow state machine (spec_required -> implementation_ready -> review_ready -> terminal), with schema-validated Spec/context/workspace provenance, pre-review verification evidence, review baseline reference, and optional durable review retry state. Atomic temp-file rename plus lock/lease/fencing protects saves; ordinary run results, optional-agent artifacts, and traces are not part of WorkflowState.

Durable resume is explicitly tested as fresh process B: implementation_ready skips Spec and reuses validated workspace; checkpoint resume from review_ready validates exact HEAD/source fingerprint, reconstructs baseline/diff, skips Worker and pre-review VERIFY, then runs independent REVIEW and persists terminal state. These are probe assertions, not evidence that every optional mechanism is independently resumable.

Workflow ownership remains with the outer harness: lease acquisition rejects concurrent owners, fencing/expiry is checked on every owned state save, and the outer invocation releases the lease. A terminal workflow cannot transition again; terminal success is forbidden before executable Spec reaches implementation_ready.

Optional read-only research subagent returns a structured EvidenceReport (findings with cited paths, observed paths, uncertainties), admitted only when cited files were actually read. It is advisory only—not Spec, permission, verification, or success. It has a six-turn budget, read/list/submit tools only, and records model/tool counts, token usage, failure reason, inspected paths, report, and outcome in the parent AgentRunResult/trace; no durable workflow record is written for it.

A2A remote impact delegation returns bounded ImpactAnalysisArtifact evidence after agent-card/protocol/interface admission, task completion, and scope/path validation. A2A records delegation/workflow/task/context IDs, remote PID, admission, send status, terminal state, artifact admission, and outcome; transport uncertainty is not retried because remote work may have started. The record is returned in implementation result and trace, not persisted into durable WorkflowState, and grantsWorkflowSuccess is hard-coded false; parent still owns implementation, VERIFY, REVIEW, and success.

The A2A server publishes submitted/working/completed-or-failed task status and an ImpactAnalysis artifact, but keeps contexts/cancellation in process-local maps and is stopped by the host after delegation. No remote task/artifact persistence or cross-process resume is implemented; this durability conclusion is based on the in-memory maps and host lifecycle, not a dedicated durability test.

Optional MCP repository reading is a host-admitted capability: the host pins protocol revision, discovers tools, applies an allowlist/schema checks (only repo_read_file, no root/credential controls), and replaces implementation direct read_file with the admitted tool. Server receives only host-configured absolute root, refuses an OPENAI_API_KEY environment, and returns text/error. MCP call evidence is trace/result-level; no durable MCP state or artifact is recorded, and outer Worker/VERIFY/REVIEW authority remains unchanged.

Verified repository memory is the one optional mechanism intentionally persisted across independent runs: successful workflow/VERIFY/review pass can produce an admitted implementation-surface record with repository scope, claim, source fingerprint, base revision, originating workflow/run, and evidence; atomic immutable files reject rewrites. Retrieval filters repository scope and revalidates current source/claim, rejecting stale records and injecting only an advisory hint. Memory cannot change WorkflowState or become authoritative; store read failures degrade to failed retrieval metrics.

Fan-out is bounded experimental execution, not durable delegation: child artifacts include workspace/base provenance, source delta, diff, verification output, repair/model/token/timing data; exact-base checks, child VERIFY, deterministic fan-in, conflict/lost-change reporting, and final gates determine success. Evidence is returned as FanOutEvidence and experiment JSON/report files, but workflow checkpoint state does not contain child artifacts or a resume protocol; default architecture remains one Worker.

Planner and review-plan/decomposition variants are advisory experiment layers. Their experiment records compare correctness, verification/repair outcomes, model/tool/token/time metrics and write JSON/report artifacts; encoded decisions keep the default architecture unchanged. The planner hypothesis explicitly says it cannot become authority, and the subagent/planner experiment code marks conclusions as candidate/reject/inconclusive rather than automatic adoption.

Retry durability is narrowly implemented for REVIEW: harness-owned classification/budget creates operation IDs and attempt counters, persists retry state in review_ready, can pause after retry admission, and resumes the same operation. Ambiguous side effects produce needs_reconciliation rather than automatic retry; model does not classify or decide. Other retry operation kinds are types/policy support, not evidence here of persisted Spec/Worker/VERIFY retries.

Trace JSONL is append-only operational evidence (events include optional-agent lifecycle, tool results, verification/review outcomes), and probes write separate invocation/evaluation reports. Traces are not transactionally coupled to durable state; claims relying on them should be treated as observational evidence rather than resumable state.

uncertainties: The read-limited run.ts was not fully inspected, so exact call sites that merge each optional record into HarnessRunResult are inferred from the declared result types/probes and mechanism modules; persistence conclusions remain limited to files directly showing stores and probes.
No dedicated test file contents were read (only the test directory listing); probe/test filenames indicate coverage exists, but pass status and assertions beyond inspected probe code are unverified.
Fan-out/planner/review-plan experiment artifact files are generated by code, but whether a particular production run actually generated them is unverified.

A2A remote service task state may be durable inside an external implementation, but this repository's spawned server has in-process task/context state only; external persistence is unsupported/unverified.
